title: At-Tawwab, the Ever-Relenting
hookLine: the Ever-Relenting, who turns toward those who turn
tomorrow: if He turns to all who turn, what about wrongs never made right?

cards: A text sits in versions for days. Two words: i'm sorry. Every hour it waits, it gets harder to send, because now it isn't only sorry for the thing.
It's sorry for the wait. Yesterday's question was whether the door still opens if you turn back late. Today's Name is the answer, and it's built for exactly this.

teach.b: At-Tawwab, the Ever-Relenting. Tawba, in Arabic, means turning back, and At-Tawwab is the One who turns toward whoever turns, and keeps doing it.
The Qur'an tells it from the very beginning, after Adam's slip, in Pickthall's words: "Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him."
On the late part, a hadith in Tirmidhi says God accepts a servant's turning until the last breath. Late isn't locked. And the welcome isn't cold.

In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, tells of a man in the desert whose camel wanders off with his food and water. He gives up and lies down to wait for death. He wakes, and it's standing right there.
God, the Prophet says, is more pleased with a servant's turning than that man with his camel. That's the one to tell a friend tonight. Now watch this week's Names fold into it.
The Last, still there at the end of the day. The Outward and the Hidden, near enough to hear a whisper of sorry. The Governor, the Exalted, the Source of Goodness.
And At-Tawwab, turning toward the one who turns.

how: Muslims make tawba by stopping a wrong, regretting it and resolving not to return to it, and, where someone was wronged, by making it right with them; they call on Allah as ya Tawwab in du'a.

o: the One who turns toward those who turn
the One who keeps score of each mistake
the One who waits for you to earn it back

games.q: what's inside the turning — tap the pairs.
p: received words, and was turned to

s: if you wait too long to turn back, the door is shut
a hadith in Tirmidhi says God accepts a servant's turning until the last breath.
the Qur'an says God relented toward Adam after his slip
"Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him."
God accepts repentance, but coldly, as a formality
the Prophet compared His pleasure to a man in the desert finding his lost camel.

games.q: your little brother broke your headphones, hid it for a week, and finally confesses. what would At-Tawwab suggest you do first?
o: turn toward him: the door stays open for someone who turns, even late.
make him wait a week too, so it all feels fair.
say it's fine but stay quietly mad; it keeps the peace.
games.why: At-Tawwab turns toward whoever turns, late included, and is glad. people aren't God, but the Name gives a direction to lean.

practice: Write one short line by hand: something you'd like to turn back from, or someone you'd like to turn back toward. Keep it private. For the sit, just hold the line, and the open door it's facing.

wordCard.voice: At-Tawwab. The Ever-Relenting: the One who turns toward those who turn, even late, and is glad when they do.

orig.note: Arabic: the Ever-Relenting, who turns toward those who turn. tawba, turning back, comes from the same root.

carryVoice: Your line: he turns to me, every time i turn. Two weeks of Names, and the door's still open.

sources.q: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him.

sources.ref: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3537 (God accepts a servant's repentance until the death rattle)
Sahih Muslim 2747 (the man in the desert who finds his lost camel); also Sahih al-Bukhari 6309
